The sample size is the largest to date for this type of study, and baseline characteristics are thoroughly described.
D1_Source_Evidence: Children aged 8–16.99 years were recruited from five paediatric emergency departments within 48 h of sustaining a concussion (n = 360; 56% male) or mild orthopaedic injury (n = 196; 62% male).
D1_Source_Reasoning: The authors clearly define the age range, recruitment source (EDs), and the nature of the injuries for both the TBI and OI groups.
D1_Method_Evidence: The A-CAP study recruited children (8–16.99 years of age) within 48 h post-injury from five children's hospital emergency departments in Canada, all members of the Pediatric Emergency Research Canada network.
D1_Method_Reasoning: Recruitment was prospective and conducted across multiple specialized pediatric centers, reducing the risk of site-specific bias.
D1_Period_Reasoning: While the protocol is referenced (Yeates et al. 2017), the specific calendar dates for the recruitment period are not explicitly stated in this manuscript.
D1_Place_Evidence: five children's hospital emergency departments in Canada... Calgary, Edmonton, Montreal, Ottawa, Vancouver
D1_Place_Reasoning: The specific cities and clinical settings (EDs) are clearly listed.
D1_Criteria_Evidence: Children with TBI sustained a blunt head trauma and met at least one of three criteria per the World Health Organization definition of mild TBI... Delayed neurological deterioration (e.g. Glasgow Coma Scale score <13), neurosurgical intervention, loss of consciousness >30 min or post-traumatic amnesia >24 h were exclusionary criteria
D1_Criteria_Reasoning: The study uses standardized WHO criteria and provides specific clinical thresholds for exclusion.
D1_Participation_Reasoning: The paper does not provide the total number of eligible patients screened versus those who consented (participation rate), making it difficult to assess potential selection bias at the point of entry.
D1_Baseline_Evidence: Table 2 Sample demographic and injury characteristics... Age, Sex, Parental education, Race, Mechanism of injury, Sport-related injury, Loss of consciousness, Glasgow Coma Scale, Prior concussion history
D1_Baseline_Reasoning: Table 2 provides a comprehensive breakdown of demographics and injury-related variables for both groups.
D2_Risk_Reasoning: Attrition rates are reported and are relatively low for a longitudinal neuroimaging study. The use of Linear Mixed Effects (LME) models helps mitigate the impact of missing data at specific time points.
D2_Response_Evidence: Overall study attrition rates (i.e. 15, 25 and 28% for the post-acute, 3- and 6-month assessments, respectively) are consistent with other studies
D2_Response_Reasoning: A 72% retention rate at 6 months is considered acceptable for this study design.
D2_Attempts_Reasoning: The paper does not describe specific efforts to re-engage or collect data from dropouts.
D2_Reasons_Evidence: the final data set included 882 scans from 556 children after excluding 241 scans (21%; 170 TBI/71 OI) during initial quality assessment due to unstandardized acquisition parameters... severe motion artefact... incomplete acquisition... scanner artefacts... or gross brain structure abnormalities.
D2_Reasons_Reasoning: The authors provide detailed reasons for data exclusion (technical/quality issues), but do not explicitly detail the behavioral or personal reasons for participant dropout.

D2_Diff_Reasoning: The authors do not explicitly state whether they tested for differences between completers and non-completers.

D3_Def_Evidence: Children with TBI sustained a blunt head trauma and met at least one of three criteria per the World Health Organization definition of mild TBI.
D3_Def_Reasoning: The primary prognostic factor (injury group) is well-defined.

D3_Validity_Reasoning: The use of CDE-recommended scales and RCI methodology ensures a reliable classification of the 'persistent symptoms' prognostic factor.
D3_Continuous_Evidence: We then used the reliable change score results to classify children with mild TBI into two groups... (i) TBI with persistent symptoms... and (ii) TBI without persistent symptoms
D3_Continuous_Reasoning: The cut-points for symptom persistence are based on a standardized statistical method (RCI) rather than arbitrary data-driven thresholds.
D3_Method_Evidence: All participants in the study completed 3 T MRI at the postacute follow-up and were randomly assigned to complete a second MRI scan at the 3 or 6 months (chronic) follow-up.
D3_Method_Reasoning: The protocol was standardized across all sites and participants.
D3_Proportion_Evidence: the final data set included 882 scans from 556 children
D3_Proportion_Reasoning: The majority of the recruited sample provided usable data for the primary analysis.
D3_Imputation_Evidence: Multiple linear mixed effects models were computed... controlling for the random effect of participant.
D3_Imputation_Reasoning: LME models are the standard approach for handling missing data in longitudinal studies as they use all available data points without requiring simple imputation.

D4_Def_Evidence: Global and local (nodal) level metrics included degree, clustering coefficient, characteristic path length, smallworldness, betweenness and degree centrality, and efficiency (for definitions and descriptions, see Table 1)

D1_Method_Evidence: patients with pmTBI (8–18 years of age) were consecutively recruited from local emergency department (ED) and urgent care settings

title: Longitudinal Assessment of White Matter Abnormalities Following Sports-Related Concussion
